public_rationale: The reviewed evaluations show continuing reliability problems and some improvements. Present failures cannot prove that reliability can never be solved, while partial improvements cannot refute that claim. No decisive general counterexample or applicable impossibility result was established.
limitations: The cited empirical study covers two benchmarks and a finite set of agents.
The distinction between intrinsic model reliability and system-level safeguards remains important.
No numerical definition of solved was supplied.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI's reliability failings can never be solved, given its inherent nature.

statement.excerpt: The biggest intrinsic failings of generative AI have to do with reliability, in a way that I believe can never be solved, given their inherent nature.
statement.document_title: AlphaProof, AlphaGeometry, ChatGPT, and why the future of AI is neurosymbolic

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that generative AI cannot overcome its general reliability problems, not merely that current systems sometimes fail.
Solved means dependable performance across varied, unfamiliar tasks, with robust error control; it does not require mathematical perfection on every conceivable input.
Given their inherent nature states the proposed explanation, not a separate event that must happen before scoring.
Narrow success using an external verifier does not by itself establish that generative AI's general reliability problem is solved.
criteria.support_condition: A sound, applicable impossibility result establishes that the relevant class of generative systems cannot achieve the stated general reliability.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A generative system demonstrably overcomes the relevant reliability failures across broad, independently tested tasks, including unfamiliar inputs and repeated trials.
